ashby:bjakcareer:12bc7213-c111-4409-8981.summary:
The original mission of BJAK is we believe people deserve smarter ways to plan, save and grow their money. This is the origin of our name.

Started in 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, its the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

Today, we are expanding ways to help people in the region — this includes spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more. Our mission is help people get more from their money every day.

We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities from our offices and remotely, who truly enjoys their work. We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about…

sections.title: The Role
paras:
We are looking for product managers to own product areas within BJAK's AI Finance.

This role is for builders who can understand users, define product direction, work with engineering and design, launch fast and keep improving after release.

sections.title: What You'll Own
bullets: Own product areas across insurance, payments, savings, investing, travel or other financial services.
Define user problems, product scope, success metrics, roadmap and launch plans.
Work with engineering, design, data, operations, compliance and business teams.
Turn complex financial products into simple, usable customer journeys.
Use data, feedback, research and production issues to improve product decisions.
Launch features, monitor performance and drive iterations.
Make trade-offs between speed, user experience, business impact, compliance and operational complexity.

sections.title: What We're Looking For
bullets: Experience as Product Manager, Product Owner, founder, growth/product operator or similar role.
Strong product sense and ability to simplify complex workflows.
Able to work with engineers and designers to ship real products.
Comfortable with metrics, user feedback, experiments and post-launch learning.
Strong writing, prioritization and stakeholder management.
High ownership and ability to drive work with limited guidance.
Experience in fintech, insurance, payments, consumer apps or high-growth products is a strong advantage.

sections.title: The Kind of Builder We Want
bullets: Starts from user problems, not feature lists.
Can make decisions with incomplete information.
Knows how to ship quickly and learn after launch.
Works well with engineering without hiding behind process.
Honest about what changed because of their work versus wider team effort.

ashby:chambercardio:db251395-32a9-4036-a.summary:
Cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of death in America. At Chamber, we're rebuilding the system for cardiology, creating a world where outcomes, not volume, define success.

We partner with independent cardiologists to help them lead population health efforts in their communities, equipping them with technology, data, and operational tools that turn complex insights into better care for patients.

Our model blends clinical expertise, thoughtful design, and a modern operating platform that connects physicians, patients, and payers. We believe that making healthcare work better requires not just better software, but better connections between the systems, people, and information that make care possible.

sections.title: Role Overview:
paras: We're looking for a Senior Product Manager to own the platform capabilities and integrations that connect Chamber to the broader healthcare ecosystem.

This is a highly technical, systems-oriented role spanning healthcare interoperability, third-party integrations, APIs, data exchange, and the shared platform infrastructure that powers our care delivery model.

You'll work across a diverse set of technologies and partners, from EHRs, health information exchanges, payer data platforms, and clinical data networks to the communication and operational services that support our day-to-day workflows, including telephony, messaging, fax, and email.

sections.title: Platform Strategy & Product Ownership
bullets: Own and evolve Chamber's roadmap for interoperability, external integrations, APIs, and supporting platform capabilities.
Translate clinical, operational, and business needs into clear product requirements, prioritized roadmaps, and actionable technical initiatives.
Identify opportunities to build reusable integration frameworks, shared services, and platform capabilities rather than relying on one-off implementations.

Partner closely with Engineering, Data, Clinical, and Operations to evaluate architectural tradeoffs, integration patterns, and build-versus-buy decisions, and to ensure integrations deliver measurable value.
Balance immediate integration needs with longer-term investments in reliability, scalability, maintainability, and operational efficiency.

sections.title: Healthcare Interoperability & Data Exchange
bullets: Lead product discovery, technical scoping, and delivery of integrations across EHRs, health information exchanges, payer systems, clinical data networks, and other healthcare technology platforms.

Develop a strong understanding of the clinical and administrative data moving through Chamber's ecosystem, including patient identity, encounters, medications, clinical records, claims, eligibility, and care coordination information.
Work with engineering and external partners to define data mappings, synchronization requirements, API contracts, and integration workflows.
Drive improvements in data completeness, accuracy, timeliness, and consistency across connected systems.
Help establish scalable approaches to data ingestion, normalization, identity resolution, reconciliation, and bidirectional synchronization.
Ensure interoperability solutions account for healthcare privacy, security, consent, and applicable regulatory requirements.

sections.title: Third-Party Integrations & Technology Partnerships
bullets: Own the product lifecycle of integrations with external technology providers, including communications platforms, workflow tools, and operational infrastructure.
Lead technical discovery and requirements gathering with prospective vendors and integration partners, evaluating capabilities, limitations, dependencies, and implementation complexity.
Work directly with partner product and engineering teams to define integration requirements, align delivery plans, and coordinate joint roadmaps.
Contribute to technical due diligence, vendor evaluation, and build-versus-buy assessments in partnership with Engineering, Security, and business stakeholders.
Identify opportunities to consolidate fragmented capabilities, reduce vendor dependencies, and improve the consistency of shared platform services.
Maintain a clear understanding of existing integrations, their capabilities, operational health, and opportunities for improvement.

ashby:clipboard:207a6c4e-bb1f-4271-b601-.summary:
Our mission is to uplift as many communities as possible. We do this through our app-based marketplace that connects healthcare professionals with the workplaces that need amazing workers. This enables hundreds of thousands of people to achieve financial stability for themselves and their families while providing essential care to millions of people across the U.S.

Founded in 2016, we are a remote-first team of over 1,000 people building a top Y-Combinator company and have been profitable since 2022. We’re the leader in Long-Term Care staffing and are rapidly expanding into Home Health, Hospitals, and more, meaning we have more work to do than people to do it, and are growing our team to support millions more people and their communities.

sections.title: About the role :
paras: An indispensable component of Clipboard's marketplace is its workplace customers. The Customer Success Manager ensures the continued success of the partnership between Clipboard and its workplace partners, working to deliver an optimal experience at every level of their organizations. The job encompasses being a resource to workplaces when issues arise, liaising with building- and corporate-level contacts, and keeping abreast of a litany of important business metrics for each account.

Your week will be balanced between high-touch customer engagement and internal account strategy, with a laser focus on net revenue retention. You are an avid problem-solver, a strategic communicator, and a diligent executor who can navigate complex relationships to sharpen your business acumen.

sections.title: Responsibilities :
bullets: Strategic account planning: Build and maintain detailed account plans. Forecast performance accurately and provide regular insights to internal leadership regarding pipeline health and account stability.

Drive executive value: Establish trust with both clinical and non-clinical executives. Lead Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs) and strategic meetings to demonstrate value, align on business goals, and negotiate mutually beneficial outcomes.
Operational excellence: Act as the primary point of contact for complex escalations, ensuring rapid resolution while implementing systemic solutions to prevent recurrence.

Cross-functional advocacy: Partner with Product, Legal, and Strategy Operations to represent the voice of the customer, driving product improvements and internal initiatives that optimize the client experience.

sections.title: Beyond the basics, what will make you successful :
bullets: Extreme ownership : The buck stops with you, no matter what anyone else did or did not do. You're self-reliant, and can get things done in the chaos that is an early-stage startup scaling quickly.
Extreme curiosity : You ask "why" 3-5 times in a row for the same problem, digging and digging and not being satisfied until you truly understand the root cause.
Scrappiness : You look for ways through problems and refuse to let obstacles derail your progress. You bring solutions instead of asking ‘what should I do?’
Fast-paced : You thrive on moving quickly and are highly adaptable to a market that evolves quickly.

sections.title: Why a case study first?
paras: Since this role is remote and requires a high degree of autonomy, the case study helps us understand how you operate in an asynchronous environment. Specifically, we’re looking at how you interpret written context, navigate ambiguity, and identify opportunities independently. This ensures our first conversation is grounded in your actual work style rather than just a resume walkthrough.

ashby:codametrix:9dc5e42c-efa8-432c-9c86.summary: CodaMetrix is revolutionizing Revenue Cycle Management with its AI-powered autonomous coding solution, a multi-specialty AI-platform that translates clinical information into accurate sets of medical codes. CodaMetrix’s autonomous coding drives efficiency under fee-for-service and value-based care models and supports improved patient care. We are passionate about getting physicians and healthcare providers away from the keyboard and back to clinical care.

sections.title: Overview
paras: The Account Director is a member of the Account Management team, owning a portfolio of client relationships and driving the adoption, retention, and growth of CodaMetrix's autonomous coding solutions. Senior Account Directors carry the same charter across a larger, higher-value portfolio, with added accountability for cross-team escalation outcomes and for developing the team.

We're looking for people who are proactive, not reactive — who surface the upsell, the risk, or the fix before a client has to ask. The strongest Account Directors are highly accountable: they treat a customer commitment as theirs to protect even when the root cause sits with another team, and they're comfortable navigating internal friction and managing customer expectations to reach the right outcome, not just the easy one.

sections.title: Responsibilities — Account Director
paras: • Growth & Retention Strategy: Execute client-specific growth strategies to increase usage and adoption, and cultivate upsell/cross-sell opportunities within existing accounts.
• Client Relationship Management: Build trusted-advisor relationships with key client stakeholders, expanding your footprint across each account in your portfolio.
• AI-Driven Insights: Scale advanced analytics into insights that help clients make data-driven decisions and see the impact of our solutions.

sections.title: Additional Responsibilities — Senior Account Director
paras: • Escalation Ownership (expanded scope): Proactively identify delivery risk before it reaches the customer, drive resolution across teams, and escalate to leadership when needed — accountable for the outcome, not just your contribution to it.
• Team Development: Mentor the team and build shared best practices that scale growth and retention across the portfolio.
• Deep Subject Matter Expertise: Develop and share expertise on industry and competitive trends to advise both clients and colleagues.

sections.title: REQUIRED
paras: • 5+ years in account management with a focus on strategic client relationships and revenue growth; 3+ years in healthcare.
• Strong analytical and critical-thinking skills, with the ability to present data and insights effectively.
• A track record of resolving risk before it reaches the client — including a willingness to navigate internal stakeholders and barriers, not just customer-facing ones, to get there.

ashby:credo.ai:aa00d1c3-d4cb-4577-ae3d-9.summary: The Credo AI Governance Platform operates as the trust layer for global enterprises focused on transforming their organizations with AI. It is powered by a knowledge graph that is updated by agents, enriched with global regulatory intelligence and curated business context, supported by Forward-Deployed Experts, giving enterprises a clear view of the risk profile behind every AI system. By making that risk visible, we enable teams to move quickly and confidently scale across systems to adopt compliant AI, faster and in a compliant manner.

sections.title: The Role
paras: While AI agents are now widely adopted, enterprise have struggled to scale their governance. Our customers need to know which agents they have, set rules for each one, make sure those rules hold where the agent runs, and prove it to auditors and regulators. That is the focus of our Agent Governance product area. You'll be its technical product manager. You'll help shape and drive the roadmap for agent governance, from agent discovery to policy operationalization to assurance.

You’ll work directly with design partners and early customers to understand their environments, define successful rollouts, and ensure the product delivers value. Working with engineering and the customer’s IT, security, and platform teams, you’ll identify and resolve adoption barriers and turn what you learn into product improvements. You’ll also work with partners and systems integrators to make deployment increasingly repeatable, and collaborate with our go-to-market team on marketing and sales enablement as the product matures.

sections.title: What You'll Do
bullets: Shape and drive the agent governance roadmap in partnership with research, engineering, and product leadership, translating customer needs and company priorities into clear monthly and quarterly outcomes.
Define measures of product success and use customer feedback and product metrics to guide prioritization.

Identify and prioritize integrations and platforms based on customer needs and market opportunity. Work with engineering to define requirements for translating governance policies into operational controls.

Work directly with design partners and early customers to scope rollouts, define success criteria, and support adoption, including hands-on configuration where appropriate. Partner with engineering and customer teams on technical implementation and security and data-handling reviews.
Develop deployment playbooks with engineering, Customer Success, and partners, including reference architectures, runbooks, and troubleshooting guidance that make deployments repeatable.
Work with technology partners on integrations and joint deployments, and keep up with relevant agent, identity, and authorization standards.
Partner with Sales, Customer Success, and Marketing on customer conversations, demos, positioning, pricing, launch, and sales enablement as the product matures.

sections.title: What Hands-On Means Here
bullets: You use and configure the product in test and design-partner environments so you understand the customer experience firsthand.
You can work through traces, logs, and configuration with engineering to understand an issue and translate what you learn into product requirements or customer guidance.
You work directly with customers’ IT, security, and platform teams during rollout, and develop the rollout playbook with engineering and Customer Success.
You build prototypes, mockups, or lightweight scripts to explore and communicate ideas where useful, partnering with engineering on technical feasibility and final implementation.

sections.title: Required:
bullets: 5+ years in technical roles, including at least 2 years of product management.
Deep experience with AI agents and coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex or similar), including how they are configured: settings, hooks, permissions and MCP servers.
Comfortable diving into API documentation and building understanding through small prototypes.
Working knowledge of identity and access management (OAuth, OIDC, SCIM; Okta or Microsoft Entra) and of at least one major cloud (AWS or Azure).

Experience shipping enterprise software in customer environments, including satisfying requirements around single sign-on, device management (Jamf or Intune), security reviews, and rollout across teams.
A track record of running technical pilots or proofs of concept with enterprise customers and turning what you learned into product.
Clear, concise writing. You can explain a technical trade-off to an engineer, a customer's security leader and a governance lead.
Comfort owning outcomes with a small team in a startup environment.

ashby:foundationhealthcareers:4acb9647-2.summary:
Foundation Health is an AI operating system for pharmacy - built by a team who lived the problem firsthand, not one that came to healthcare from the outside. Every day, prior authorizations delay prescriptions, pharmacists lose hours to paperwork instead of patients, and prescriptions slip through the cracks between health systems. We believe thoughtfully applied AI can finally change that - deep, integrated infrastructure that streamlines how care is coordinated, purpose-built for the complexity of specialty pharmacy.

We're building toward a world where pharmacy teams spend their time on patients, not paperwork - where AI handles the routine so clinicians can focus on what only humans can do. Getting there takes the right people. We're looking for curious, ambitious folks who want to help solve healthcare's hardest problems - for our patients, our partners, and each other.

sections.title: The Role:
paras: Somewhere along the way, work got predictable. The problems arrive pre-scoped, the interesting decisions happen somewhere above you, and the thing you're actually good at - figuring things out - is the thing you get to do least.
You'd be our second US Product hire - real 0-1 building in a fully AI-native company, shipping AI products into healthcare, at a pace where your decisions go live in days.

And while nobody here will scope your work for you, you'll be surrounded by people worth learning from: an ex-DeepMind VP of Engineering, and an experienced Product Director with deep domain expertise who's seen this space from every angle.

sections.title: What you'll actually do:
paras: Honestly? Things we can't fully explain how to do - because nobody's done them yet. That's the job.

One thing we won't do is hold your hand. The problems arrive ambiguous, there's no playbook, and nobody will scope your work for you. If that sounds like the appeal rather than the risk — keep reading.
bullets: Take genuinely ambiguous problems ("patients keep dropping off between prescription and refill - fix it") and figure out what gets built and why
Ship AI products - AI isn't a feature we bolted on, it's what we build and how we work
Do real discovery - talk to customers, pharmacists and patients, then come back with a point of view
Work daily with Engineering and Design; you'll be in the detail, not above it
Make the case, not just the product - the best PMs here can put numbers behind "why this, why now"
Move fast. Our cycle times are days and weeks, not quarters, and your decisions go live

sections.title: Who thrives here?
bullets: Smart generalists who figure things out. You don't need to have done this exact job before. You need to be the person who, given a problem no one's solved and no instructions, just starts solving it - and enjoys it.
High-agency owners. You don't wait to be told, you don't need work scoped for you, and you're at your best when something is genuinely yours - your call, your build, your consequences.

People who are already AI-obsessed. You don't need to have shipped AI products professionally. But AI is probably already stitched into your day - drafting, triaging, building little things on the side, whatever you've rigged up - and you're learning in your own time because you can't help it. That's how we work too.
Clear communicators. We move quickly, which only works when people get to the point - with engineers, with customers, with each other. If you can make a complex thing simple, you'll do well here.

The endlessly curious. You're the person who's always got ideas, who reads about things outside your lane, who'd turn up to a conversation with us having already poked around how prescriptions actually work. No healthcare experience needed - just genuine hunger to learn a messy, regulated, fascinating space.
People who want the startup pace. Small team, short cycles, real ownership, no ceiling. If that sounds energising rather than terrifying, you're our kind of person.

ashby:harvey:35bd9daf-d303-4312-8145-e9b.summary:
At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we…

sections.title: Why Harvey
paras: At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

sections.title: Role Overview
paras: Harvey’s Legal Engineer - Product Specialists are experienced lawyers from leading asset managers who leverage their legal expertise to help in-house legal and compliance teams at asset managers to seamlessly integrate Harvey into their daily workflows, drive adoption, increase utilization, and support long-term expansion and renewal. Legal Engineer - Product Specialists collaborate closely with Harvey’s Customer Success Managers and Account Executives to drive all facets of the post-sales strategy. They develop consultative relationships with innovation teams, internal AI committees and in-house teams at asset managers, serving as trusted advisors on how Harvey’s AI solutions can enhance legal effectiveness and efficiency.

Legal Engineer - Product Specialists draw on their legal training and practice experience to ask thoughtful questions, uncover adoption barriers, and develop tailored strategies that build credibility with customers. They partner with Customer Success Managers and Account Executives to communicate Harvey’s value through a mix of large group sessions, small workshops, and one-on-one conversations.

You will be among the first members of our new asset management team, with the opportunity to decide how customers in this space adopt Harvey and where it delivers the most value. You will work directly with their in-house legal teams, and your feedback will help shape the product through the lens of someone who has done the job before.

sections.title: What You’ll Do
bullets: Help shape how asset management customers use Harvey and get value from it. As part of a dedicated team, you will define the use cases, workflows, and enablement approaches for this customer segment.

Build trusted relationships with in-house legal teams at asset managers by understanding their unique workflows and offering tailored guidance on how to incorporate Harvey’s AI into their daily practice.
Design and lead onboarding sessions, training workshops, and ongoing enablement programs that drive adoption and maximize the value of Harvey’s platform.
Act as a strategic partner to Customer Success Managers and Account Executives to identify expansion opportunities and support renewal efforts through demonstrated impact and engagement.
Proactively surface obstacles to adoption by engaging users with thoughtful questions and legal empathy, then develop and implement strategies to overcome them.
Translate legal practice needs into actionable feedback for the product and engineering teams, helping to shape product development through a lawyer’s lens.
Monitor usage trends and identify at-risk accounts or untapped opportunities, working cross-functionally to re-engage users and showcase new or underutilized capabilities.
Contribute to customer-facing content (e.g., training materials, use case guides, FAQ resources) to ensure continued customer success across customer teams.

sections.title: What You Have
bullets: JD or equivalent legal qualification (including non-US qualifications).
3 years+ of experience practicing law in-house at an asset manager.
Executive engagement skills and presence, with an ability to establish strong relationships with key decision makers and build credibility at all levels.
Outstanding presentation skills to both legal and executive audiences, whether impromptu on a whiteboard or using presentations and demos.
Strong understanding of legal processes and challenges faced by legal professionals at asset managers.
Curiosity about AI’s potential to transform the legal industry.
Desire to build agents and design workflows to optimize routine tasks.
Entrepreneurial mindset, with comfort building new programs and approaches from scratch.

ashby:horizon3ai:f8146886-3fb1-4c85-bb88.summary: Horizon3 is a fast-growing, remote cybersecurity company dedicated to the mission of enabling organizations to proactively find and fix and verify exploitable attack vectors before criminals exploit them. Our flagship product, the NodeZeroTM platform, delivers production-safe autonomous pentests and other key assessment operations that scale across the largest internal, external, cloud, and hybrid cloud environments. NodeZero has been adopted by organizations of all sizes, from small educational institutions to government agencies and Global 100 enterprises. It is used by ITOps/SecOps teams, consulting pentesters, and MSSPs and MSPs.

sections.title: Get to Know Us
paras: We are a fusion of former U.S. Special Operations cyber operators, startup engineers, and formerly frustrated cybersecurity practitioners. We're committed to helping solve our common security problems: ineffective security tools, false positives resulting in alert fatigue, blind spots, "checkbox” security culture, cybersecurity skills shortage, and the long lead time and expense of hiring outside consultants. Collectively, we are a team of learn it alls, committed to a culture of respect, collaboration, ownership, and results.

sections.title: About the Role
paras: Horizon3 is in search of a highly motivated and technically skilled Staff Product Manager to lead the strategy and evolution of NodeZero Rapid Response. This role requires a strong blend of product leadership, cybersecurity expertise, threat intelligence experience, technical depth, and customer empathy to help organizations quickly understand whether emerging vulnerabilities create real, exploitable risk in their environments.

The Staff Product Manager for Rapid Response will own the product strategy, roadmap, customer experience, and operating model for NodeZero Rapid Response. This leader will partner closely with the Attack Team, Engineering, Data, Design, Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Channel, and Support to define how Horizon3 monitors emerging threats, determines which vulnerabilities matter, maps those threats to customer environments, validates real-world exploitability, and helps customers take action before attackers do.

sections.title: Rapid Response Product Strategy & Leadership
bullets: Own the product vision, strategy, roadmap, and measurable outcomes for NodeZero Rapid Response, helping customers understand and respond to emerging vulnerabilities based on real exploitability and customer-specific risk.

Establish the end-to-end operating model for Rapid Response, from initial threat signal through research, prioritization, customer relevance analysis, exploit/test development, notification, remediation, retesting, and verification.
Set clear ownership, decision rights, service-level expectations, and operating rhythms across the teams required to deliver Rapid Response at speed.
Drive standardization and scalability across Rapid Response research, customer communications, integrations, and operational workflows.

sections.title: Exploit Intelligence & Coverage Strategy
bullets: Establish and grow exploit-intelligence relationships with security vendors, researchers, and other relevant intelligence providers to identify emerging Rapid Response opportunities as early as possible.

Define the threat intelligence strategy for Rapid Response across vendor advisories, CVEs, CISA KEV, public research, exploit repositories, attacker activity, and other sources of vulnerability and exploit intelligence.

Develop a prioritization framework for determining which vulnerabilities warrant immediate Rapid Response coverage based on exploitability, attacker utility, prevalence, customer footprint, potential impact, and evidence of exploitation in the wild.

Partner directly with vulnerability researchers and attack engineers to assess exploit prerequisites, affected products and versions, attack techniques, mitigations, and the evidence and production-safety controls needed to validate exploitability in customer environments.

ashby:hyperexponential:d8f72d39-e39a-44a.summary:
At hyperexponential, we’re building the AI-powered platform that enables the world’s most critical decisions in a $7 trillion industry - which risks to take, and how to price them. These are the decisions that shape real-world outcomes: whether rockets successfully launch into space, autonomous vehicles make it to market, or communities recover after major storms.

Until now, insurance has been making billion-dollar decisions using outdated tools. We’re changing that. Our platform brings together data, AI, and human expertise to give insurers the fastest path from submission to decision - helping them move faster, act smarter, and take on more risk with confidence.

sections.title: About hyperexponential (hx)
paras: Backed by a16z, Highland Europe, and Battery Ventures, we’re scaling globally - already trusted by nearly 50 of the world’s largest insurers, with zero churn and billions in premiums flowing through hx.

What began as a single product in one market has rapidly evolved into a multi-product, multi-territory platform powering every stage of pricing and underwriting. AI is at the core of what we do - from building the world’s first domain-specific AI peer programmer for insurance (think GitHub Copilot with a PhD in actuarial science) to shaping agentic workflows that reinvent how this industry operates.

What makes hx different is the people who build it. Here, impact isn’t tied to title or tenure; it’s defined by the challenges you take on and the discipline you bring. Surrounded by peers who stretch you, you’ll do the best, hardest work of your life in a company engineered to endure.

sections.title: About the Solutions Engineering team
paras: Solutions Engineering at hx is the technical heart of our go-to-market organisation. This team is responsible for the Technical Win - convincing underwriters, actuaries, IT leaders, and security teams that hx is the platform they can trust with the pricing and underwriting decisions that define their business.

Our Solution Engineers sit at the edge of what’s possible for our product, our customers, and our industry. This is a small, senior team working on the hardest and most interesting problems hx encounters - where only a combination of technical depth, market expertise, and Renew knowledge will do.

As a Solutions Engineer, you are often one of the first hxers a prospect meets. Every engagement is high-stakes. Every interaction is visible. You help customers reimagine how pricing and underwriting can work, turning bold ideas and messy legacy realities into practical, production-ready solutions that actually ship. You leave a trace that shapes how customers see the entire company.

sections.title: What you’ll be doing
bullets: Own the technical sales motion for complex opportunities, driving the technical win across discovery, demos, proofs of value, and technical evaluations - leveraging AI-assisted process
Design and deliver high-impact, persona-led demos for actuaries, underwriters, IT, and executive stakeholders, showing both the power of hx Renew and the art of the possible
Run technically ambitious POVs , often innovating at the edge of hx Renew’s capabilities to address complex or novel customer use cases
Act as a trusted technical advisor throughout the sales process, contributing meaningfully to RFPs and RFIs, answering deep technical questions, handling objections
Rapidly build deep expertise in hx Renew, Python-based workflows, insurance pricing and AI use cases becoming a credible technical authority with customers and internal teams
Feed real-world customer insight back into Product and Engineering, helping shape future platform capabilities based on emerging customer needs and emerging AI use cases

sections.title: What you’ll need to have done
bullets: You must have extensive experience coding in Python
Experience as an Actuary, Underwriter or Technical Broker
Exposure to technical, customer-facing work within a B2B SaaS, technology, or data-driven environment (this could include internships, placements, graduate roles, or early-career positions)
Experience supporting or observing multi-stakeholder conversations , where technical considerations needed to be explained, justified, or adapted for different audiences
Demonstrated ability to build, adapt, or explain technical artefacts (e.g. demos, scripts, prototypes, analyses, workflows), even if not owned end-to-end in a sales context
Evidence of earning trust through clear communication, curiosity, and follow-through , whether with customers, internal stakeholders, or project partners
A strong sense of ownership and collaboration , with examples of working closely with peers across technical and non-technical functions to move work forward

ashby:intus:d266bc7c-cb0b-492c-a23e-90dc.summary:
About IntusCare:
IntusCare is the only end-to-end technology ecosystem built specifically for PACE (Programs of All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly) and similar coordinated care models. We help our customers deliver exceptional care, strengthen financial performance, and stay compliant through a purpose-built EMR and a suite of modern, cloud-native solutions where data and AI sit at the center of everything we do. The result: modern infrastructure for complex senior care, so teams spend less time wrestling with systems and more time caring for older adults with the dignity they deserve.

sections.title: Role Overview:
paras: The Senior Account Manager serves as the strategic relationship owner for a portfolio of IntusCare clients and is directly responsible for commercial growth within their book of business. This person will blend commercial and sales acumen with a deep commitment to partnership, ensuring every client realizes the full value of IntusCare’s solutions while identifying and closing opportunities for renewal, expansion and long-term growth.
You’ll work hand-in-hand with our Sales, Client Success, Implementation, Product, and other Client Delivery teams to drive value, retention, and growth across your accounts.

sections.title: Key Responsibilities:
bullets: Identify and pursue opportunities to expand IntusCare’s footprint through cross-sell and upsell strategies
Serve as the primary commercial contact for assigned clients, managing renewals, upsells, and contract negotiations in partnership with leadership
Develop and maintain strong, trust-based relationships with executive and operational stakeholders across client organizations
Monitor and be responsible for overall account health and proactively address risks or barriers to client satisfaction in conjunction with other cross-functional teams

Serve as the voice of the customer internally by building trusted, cross-functional relationships across Product, Client Delivery, Analytics, and other key teams - becoming a go-to connector who routes client needs efficiently to the right stakeholders
Lead quarterly business reviews and strategic planning sessions with clients
Collaborate internally with Product and Analytics teams to communicate client needs, feature requests, and success stories
Maintain accurate records of account activity, renewal timelines, and pipeline opportunities in CRM and project systems

sections.title: Requirements:
paras: The base salary range for this role is 130K-145K. We expect the ideal candidate to fall near the midpoint of this range, though final compensation will be determined based on experience, skills, and organizational needs.
Work location : This is a fully remote role based in the United States.
Sponsorship : This position is not eligible for sponsorship.
bullets: 4-8+ years of experience in account management, client partnerships, sales or commercial roles within healthcare technology, population health or SaaS environments

ashby:pivotal-health:24a633ce-b532-40a8-.summary:
Pivotal Health is the leading technology platform that helps healthcare providers get paid fairly in an increasingly complex reimbursement landscape.

Today, many providers face persistent underpayment from health insurance companies, despite delivering high-quality care. While processes like IDR (Independent Dispute Resolution) were designed to promote fairness, they’re often administrative-heavy, time-consuming, and difficult to navigate without the right tools.

Pivotal Health combines software, data, and service into a seamlessly integrated, AI-driven platform that simplifies these complex reimbursement workflows. We help providers efficiently dispute underpaid claims, reduce administrative burden, and recover the reimbursement they’re entitled to; without adding more work to already stretched teams.

sections.title: About Pivotal Health
paras: Our full-service IDR solution is just the starting point. We’re building solutions that enable providers to operate with clarity, control, and confidence across the reimbursement journey.

sections.title: About the Role
paras: Physician groups are the core of Pivotal Health's business. Emergency Medicine, Anesthesiology, Radiology and other specialty groups trust us to recover out-of-network revenue through the federal and state IDR process. How they experience us decides whether they stay, expand, and refer to their peers.

As Head of Client Success, Physician Groups, you'll lead the largest team in Client Success: the pod leads and CSMs who own every physician group relationship in our direct book. You build deep relationships with our clients, foster trust and coach the team on relationship building. You own retention for that book. That means identifying improvement areas before the client tells us, and running a structured stabilization motion. It also means every CSM knows their client well enough to advocate for them inside Pivotal Health.

This is not a steady-state seat. The team has grown fast, and we're building its infrastructure now: health scoring, tiering, playbooks, escalation and concession frameworks, and product enablement. You'll lead that rollout and hold the team to it. You report to the Head of Client Success and sit on the CS leadership team.

Own and be accountable to gross and net retention for the physician group book. Set the targets, report on them weekly with trend and context, and answer for the number.
Build and run the at-risk motion with your team to drive continued client health motion
Lead and develop pod leads and CSMs. Set clear performance expectations, run real 1:1s, and make the hard calls on performance when they're needed.
Know the top accounts personally. Serve as executive sponsor for strategic groups and own the room with a group's CEO, CFO, practice administrator, or medical director.

Be the client's advocate inside Pivotal Health. Turn what clients tell us into prioritized asks for Product, Operations, and Finance, stay close during the implementation process, then close the loop with the client when it ships.

Roll out CS infrastructure across every pod: client health score, account tiering, playbooks, QBR standards, and Salesforce hygiene. The client experience should be consistent no matter who the CSM is.
Translate IDR and operational changes (MIV thresholds, batching, CMS fee changes, invoicing) into clear client communication. Make sure CSMs deliver it before clients hear it anywhere else.

ashby:pylon:22e70a73-03ee-464c-8007-202c.summary:
America’s $13T mortgage market is one of the most important financial systems in the world. It underwrites the middle class and is the mechanism through which millions of families build wealth. But while every other financial instrument has been simplified to an API call, mortgages are still assembled by hand.

We started from zero and created the first vertically integrated mortgage platform that turns origination into a single API.

Publicly traded companies and the country’s largest originators are already building on Pylon. Revenue is compounding monthly. We’re backed by Peter Thiel, Conversion Capital, QED, Citi, Fifth Wall, and the founders of Ramp, Blend, and Mercury.

sections.title: About Pylon
paras: Working at Pylon isn’t for those seeking comfort. The people who thrive here have high agency, strong opinions, and a track record of delivering outcomes without direction. Many of us are former founders. We move quickly, challenge each other directly, and take full ownership of results. It’s hard work, but it will be worth it.
Join us in building America’s mortgage rails .

sections.title: About the role
paras: For most families, a mortgage is the biggest financial decision they’ll ever make, and the process is still confusing, slow, and stressful. Loan officers don’t have it much better. They’re jumping between systems, chasing documents, and answering the same status questions over and over.

We’re hiring a Lead PM to own Customer Experience at Pylon, which covers the borrower application, the borrower dashboard, and the loan officer experience. This is where people actually see and feel what our platform can do, whether customers use our interfaces directly or embed them in their own products.
The goal is to make getting a mortgage feel easy. Borrowers should always know where they stand and what’s next, and loan officers should spend their time helping borrowers instead of pushing paper.

sections.title: What you’ll do
bullets: Set the direction for every borrower and loan officer experience at Pylon, get product, design, and engineering aligned on it, and help grow the team as it scales
Own the roadmap for the borrower application, borrower dashboard, and loan officer experience
Build an application that only asks what it needs to, fills in whatever we can get automatically, and gets borrowers to a decision faster than anyone else
Keep borrowers up to date throughout the loan, with status, next steps, outstanding items, documents, disclosures, and closing, so they never have to call and ask what’s going on
Design the loan officer experience around the work that matters most, like managing their pipeline, talking with borrowers, running pricing scenarios, and resolving issues quickly
Make every experience configurable and brandable, so customers can offer something great under their own name
Own the funnel, including conversion, drop-off, time to submit, time to close, and satisfaction, and run experiments to keep improving it
Build compliance into the experience, including disclosures, consent, adverse action notices, and accessibility, while keeping things clear for the people using it

sections.title: About you
bullets: You have strong opinions and you’ll defend them. We argue about decisions a lot here, and we’ll ask you to explain your thinking and stand behind it. We also expect you to change your mind when someone shows you you’re wrong.

You’re ruthless about priorities. Every customer has a feature request and every screen could be better. You focus on what improves the experience most, and you’re comfortable saying no to good ideas that come at the wrong time.

You’re comfortable in a heavily regulated market. Compliance is non-negotiable for us. We work with regulators to push the industry forward and get better outcomes for borrowers. We play by the rules, and we play to win.
You care a lot about borrowers, loan officers, and the lenders who serve them, and you hold a high bar for them. You notice the small things other people miss.

You default to software over manual work. One of our guiding principles is that anything in the backend mortgage process done by a human is a bug, and every status call or manual follow-up tells you the product could be doing more. When we need a temporary workaround, you flag it, write it down, and push for the real fix.

You’re good with people. You’ll work with design, engineering, customers, and the loan officers who use your product every day, and you know how to build real relationships and get results through them.
You have a lot of ideas. You notice things that could be better about the product and the team, and we’ll give you room to act on them.
You’re willing to get into the weeds. You can learn mortgage quickly, to the point where you sound like you’ve been in the industry for 20 years.

sections.title: The Team:
paras: This role is to join a "tip of the spear" team that brought Alpaca's ITN to market. We focus on building bleeding edge products that push the envelope for the entire industry. Alpaca's ITN is the world's first and only example of multimodal clearing, we invented the category. You will be joining a winning team that takes products from zero to one in the most authentic sense of the phrase with a track record to prove it. Expectations of excellence and technical competence are extremely high. This is not just any team at Alpaca, this is an elite squad of seasoned serial entrepreneurs with high agency responsible for the very innovations that generate Alpaca's competitive edge.

As Lead Product Manager, Multimodal Clearing, you will define and build a new category of market infrastructure: a multimodal clearinghouse that nets and mitigates settlement failures across the traditional and tokenized forms of the same security, across venues, token standards, and blockchains. Tokenized equities trade in isolated venues today and depend on market makers pre-funding inventory everywhere they quote. You will own the product that brings post-trade settlement, multilateral netting, and in-kind convertibility to onchain markets, so liquidity can move freely between tradfi and defi. The product builds on Alpaca's Instant Tokenization Network (ITN), which already lets participants mint and redeem tokenized equities against their traditional counterparts instantly and 24/7 within Alpaca. Your job is to take that model industry-wide: an open clearing standard and technology layer that licensed clearinghouses use to serve clearing members, broker-dealers, tokenization agents and token issuers, trading venues and ATSs, onchain RFQ and intent protocols, bridges, market makers, transfer agents, and CSDs. You will work hand in hand with clearinghouse leadership, engineering, risk, legal, compliance, operations, and with external partners and regulators. We're looking for someone who knows how clearing really works (novation, netting, margin, collateral, default management, settlement cycles) and how blockchains really work (smart contracts, oracles, vaults, cross-chain messaging), and who can turn a whitepaper into a shipped, regulated product. You are as comfortable walking a clearing member or regulator through a default scenario as you are reviewing a smart contract design with engineers.

Design the clearing mechanics with risk and engineering: a 24/7 settlement cycle, the multilateral netting engine, margin and haircuts for collateral pledged onchain (“in the net”) and offchain (“outside the net”)

greenhouse:flowfuse:6254067004.summary:
FlowFuse is the enterprise platform that bridges physical assets and enterprise IT. Built on Node-RED, it lets industrial teams unify real-time data through workflows, AI agents, and industrial applications, extending rigid vendor systems with a low-code agility layer that adapts without rip-and-replace. Our customers run factories, energy grids, and supply chains on what we ship. When we get the platform wrong, a production line feels it.

We need someone to own the FlowFuse platform outright: the solution-agnostic foundation every customer solution is built on. That means enterprise management, edge and cloud deployment, industrial connectivity, industrial data modeling and contextualization, security, operator experience, and the reusable AI/ML capabilities that will set us apart. You decide where the platform goes over the next few years, and you write the work that gets it there.

sections.title: What you'll actually do
bullets: Learn our customers and the IIoT domain fast, then keep learning. Run continuous discovery. Sit in on sales and customer calls, mine the recordings in Fathom for the problem behind the request, and talk to users directly.

Shape AI/ML in the platform. Lead the product direction for reusable AI/ML capabilities (AI-assisted development, agentic workflows, industrial data reasoning, machine vision integration), with clear judgment about what's production-ready versus a promising demo.

Make the platform enterprise-ready. Make it easier for customers and solution engineers to build, deploy, govern, and operate distributed Node-RED applications across many sites, mixed equipment, and cloud or self-hosted environments.
Run the lane day to day. Triage the backlog and every new idea that flies in, prioritize ruthlessly, sequence it, and get it into sprints.
Write GitHub issues your engineers respect. Precise, technical, unambiguous, with testable acceptance criteria. They should never have to guess what "done" means.
Run refinement with engineering. Show up prepared, make the calls, unblock fast, and validate outcomes after release.

Know the split. Product owns the roadmap, the what, and the why, and writes the issues. Engineering owns the how, technical design, and delivery estimates. Scope and sequencing tradeoffs are made together. There's no classic PM / designer / engineer trio here. It's mostly you and the engineers.
Wear other hats. This is a small startup. Some weeks the highest-leverage thing you can do isn't in your job description. You do it anyway.

sections.title: The harder part of the job
paras: Leadership here moves fast and thinks out loud. Ideas arrive at high volume and high velocity, from the CEO, our investors, your peers, and the live customer deals sales is racing to close. Part of the job is to be the filter and the translation layer. Absorb that energy, turn it into a clear and sequenced plan, and protect the engineering team's focus so they can do their best work. You don't pass chaos through. You stop it at your desk.

You'll partner closely with Solutions Engineering, who own customer solutions, industry-specific applications, and solution packaging. They are your most important internal customer. A big part of being effective is turning their field requests into platform capabilities that serve many solutions, not one, without the team feeling whiplash.
You'll also work with our CTO on technical direction and the Node-RED ecosystem. The CTO leads the Node-RED open-source project. You can advocate for upstream changes, but you don't own that project.

sections.title: Where this goes
paras: You start as a product team of one, owning the platform and doing the groundwork yourself. You may stay a team of one for a while, and we'd rather say that up front. From day one, you bring a point of view on where the platform should go. We're hiring someone to shape the plan, not just execute the one they inherit. Prove you can run it, and the path opens: take on more of the product surface, build and lead a product team, and help shape the wider product vision for FlowFuse. This scope is additive, not a graduation. A bigger title doesn't mean your baseline changes, at least not until you've built a team. We're putting that in writing because we mean it.

sections.title: Your first 90 days
bullets: Day 60. You own the platform backlog and a published, prioritized roadmap. Your engineers trust your tickets enough to stop asking what you meant. You've stood up the field-to-platform intake process with Solutions Engineering and made real calls on what becomes platform and what doesn't.

We're building a future for the Internet that's easy, sensible, and safe, like it used to be. sections.title: About the Role
paras: We are seeking a Product Manager to own Tailscale's networking features — the layer that decides how traffic finds its destination by name on top of Tailscale’s seamless mesh connectivity solution. Concretely, you will own four feature sets: App Connectors , DNS , Funnel , and Tailscale Serve & Services .

A tailnet gives every device an identity and an address. Networking features are what turn addresses into something a person, a script, or an AI agent can actually use — a name, a service, an app, a URL.

This is the most user-visible role in Tailscale's Dataplane Platform, and the work is as much product design as it is networking. DNS settings, connector topologies, and service definitions are configured by network engineers and IT admins in the admin console, API, and CLI, and the distance between "magical" and "unusable" is the object model, the defaults, and the error messages.
bullets: App Connectors route traffic to specific SaaS and private applications by name, so access follows the app rather than the IP.
DNS — MagicDNS, split DNS, custom name servers, search domains

Tailscale Serve & Services make a workload — not a machine — the unit of connectivity and access: addressable, load-balanced, and durable across the instances behind it. This is the wedge that lets customers replace a service registry, and eventually much of what they use a service mesh for, with Tailscale.
Funnel is Tailscale's ingress story: securely exposing a Service running inside the tailnet to the public internet, from a hobbyist sharing a dev server to production webhooks and public endpoints.

sections.title: Key Responsibilities
bullets: Own the vision, strategy, and roadmap for Tailscale's networking features: App Connectors, DNS, Funnel, and Tailscale Services

Shape the core platform workflows and experiences that teams across the organization rely on at enterprise scale

sections.title: About Tanium
paras: Tanium — Agentic Defense at Machine Speed. IT and security operators can’t protect what they can’t see, and they can’t fix what they haven’t found. Tanium closes that gap with real-time visibility and machine-speed control of endpoints, bringing security operations, exposure management, endpoint management, and Tanium Integrations together on a single unified agentic platform.

The full power of the platform is unleashed with Tanium Atlas, the agentic intelligence layer. Atlas connects to external data sources and AI models, turning real-time truth into governed action, with a single operator able to control millions of devices in seconds using natural language prompts and a generative user interface.

The company is recognized as a Leader in the inaugural 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Endpoint Management Tools, as a Leader in the IDC MarketScape: Worldwide Client Endpoint Management Software for Windows Device Management 2025–2026 Vendor Assessment, and as a Leader in The Forrester Wave™: Endpoint Management Platforms, Q2 2026.

sections.title: On a mission. Together.
paras: At Tanium, we are stewards of a culture that emphasizes the importance of collaboration, respect, and diversity. In our pursuit of revolutionizing the way some of the largest enterprises and governments in the world solve their most difficult IT challenges, we are strengthened by our unique perspectives and by our collective actions.

As a global organization with stakeholders around the world, it’s imperative that the diversity of our customers and communities is reflected internally in our team members. We strive to create a diverse and inclusive environment where everyone feels they have opportunities to succeed and grow because we know that only together can we do great things.
Our commitment to excellence and innovation has earned us a place on the Forbes Cloud 100 list for ten consecutive years, and we continue to be recognized worldwide as a great place to work.

greenhouse:tines:6220817004.summary:
Tines is the complete environment for enterprise AI, trusted by organizations like Reddit, SAP, Mars, Fin, and Headspace. Tines gives all teams a safe, scalable way to turn their expertise into software, whatever their technical background.

sections.title: What will you be doing?
bullets: Lead and develop a team of Renewal Managers, providing coaching, commercial guidance, and clear direction to drive strong customer and business outcomes.
Own renewal performance across the portfolio, with accountability for Gross Revenue Retention, renewal rate, churn and contraction outcomes, and on-time renewal execution.
Establish and maintain a consistent renewal forecast, providing leadership with clear visibility into renewal timing, risk, expected outcomes, and areas requiring intervention.
Guide Renewal Managers through complex customer negotiations involving pricing, contract terms, multi-year agreements, competitive pressure, procurement, and other commercial challenges.
Ensure renewal engagement begins early and that Renewal Managers have the customer context, risk signals, value realization, and relationship insights required to execute effectively.

Partner closely with Customer Success to ensure clear ownership between customer outcomes and commercial renewal execution, with CSMs focused on value, adoption, relationships, and risk mitigation while Renewals leads the commercial renewal process.
Collaborate with Sales and Account Management to identify and coordinate expansion opportunities associated with renewal cycles while maintaining clear ownership across teams.
Partner with Revenue Operations to improve renewal forecasting, CRM workflows, dashboards, automation, reporting, and operational discipline.

sections.title: What will you bring with you?
bullets: 7+ years of experience in SaaS, enterprise software, Customer Success, Account Management, Renewals, Sales, or a similar commercial customer-facing environment.
3+ years of people leadership experience, with a demonstrated track record of coaching and developing high-performing customer-facing or commercial teams.
Experience owning or managing a meaningful recurring revenue portfolio and delivering against retention or renewal targets.
A strong understanding of SaaS business metrics including ARR, Gross Revenue Retention, Net Revenue Retention, churn, contraction, renewal rate, and expansion.
Experience building and managing renewal forecasts with a high degree of operational rigor and predictability.
Strong commercial judgment and experience navigating pricing, negotiation, procurement, contracting, and customer objections.
The ability to coach teams through complex commercial situations while balancing customer relationships, revenue protection, and long-term business value.
Experience working closely with Customer Success and Sales teams to coordinate customer strategy and commercial outcomes.

sections.title: What success looks like
paras: In this role, you will build a Renewals organization that creates greater predictability for the business and a simpler, more consistent experience for customers.

Your team will engage customers earlier, identify and address risk before renewals become reactive, execute commercial conversations with confidence, and provide accurate visibility into renewal outcomes. Customer Success teams will be able to remain focused on driving value, adoption, strategic relationships, and risk mitigation while Renewal Managers bring dedicated commercial expertise to the renewal process.

At the same time, you will help Tines develop a renewal motion that can scale with the business combining strong talent, clear ownership, operational discipline, automation, and data to improve retention and strengthen long-term customer relationships.

The school that’s alerted to a threat in real-time and triggers a lockdown in seconds, not minutes. NeuralMesh™ combines high-performance data storage and extended GPU memory in a single software platform, providing a foundation for training, inference, and agentic AI workloads that maximizes GPU productivity, accelerates AI outcomes, and improves the economics of AI at scale.

WEKA is a pre-IPO, growth-stage company backed by world-class venture capital investors and AI infrastructure leaders. Our technology is trusted by 30% of the Fortune 50, as well as leading hyperscalers, neoclouds, AI builders, and research organizations. Our team is customer-obsessed, accountable, bold, and collaborative, with a shared focus on helping customers succeed. If we sound like your kind of people, join us!

sections.title: About The Role
paras: WEKA is seeking a Senior Product Marketing Manager to help define and build our AI inference business, one of the fastest-moving and most consequential markets in technology. You'll own WEKA's inference proposition for the organizations that run inference at scale, including the AI clouds and service providers that deliver it to others.

This is an early-stage product marketing role focused on a market, not a single product. You'll define how WEKA wins in inference across the full NeuralMesh portfolio. That starts with Augmented Memory Grid, which extends GPU memory and changes the economics of serving models at scale, and extends to NeuralMesh Axon, model-weight loading and checkpointing, and agentic data services. You'll help decide where WEKA should focus, who we build for, and what makes us different by discovering what customers need, testing positioning in the market, and turning what works into proof and a go-to-market motion that can scale.

Reporting to the VP of Product Marketing, you'll work closely with Product, Engineering, Sales, Solutions Engineering, Alliances, and Marketing, and alongside WEKA's Platform, Technical, Partner, Compete, and Industry product marketers. You'll also work directly with the early customers and design partners who run inference at scale: AI-native companies and model builders, enterprises putting AI into production, and the AI clouds and service providers that deliver inference to others.

sections.title: Who We're Looking For
paras: You're a product marketer who loves the early stage. You'd rather help shape a new market proposition and find the path to scale than optimize a playbook that's already working. You combine strong product marketing fundamentals with the technical depth to understand how inference really works: serving frameworks, KV cache, GPU memory hierarchies, time-to-first-token, multitenant GPU infrastructure, and the tradeoffs that set cost per token. You can go deep with an ML infrastructure engineer in the morning and build an economic argument for a CFO in the afternoon.

You're a builder who is comfortable with a blank page and an evolving answer. You treat positioning, segments, and use cases as hypotheses to test, not conclusions to defend, and you change direction quickly when the evidence says to. You're an excellent writer and storyteller who can turn an early customer result into proof, and you'd rather show specific numbers and named customers than make broad claims.

You also know that positioning only matters if it helps find and win the right customers. You stay close to customers, Product, and the market, and you watch how inference architectures, buyers, competitors, and budgets are changing. You measure success by early customer impact and by building the repeatable motion that follows.

sections.title: What You'll Be Working On
bullets: Inference Positioning & Messaging: Define WEKA's positioning, messaging, value propositions, priority use cases, and competitive differentiation for AI inference across the portfolio. Treat them as hypotheses at first, and sharpen them into one differentiated proposition as patterns emerge.
Design Partners & Early Customers: Work with Product and Sales to find, recruit, and support design partners and early adopters, and learn from every engagement.

Inference Economics: Define and quantify WEKA’s economic value across GPU utilization, time-to-first-token, throughput, concurrency, tokens per GPU, and cost per token. Build the economic case customers need to justify investment.
Proof & Evidence: Partner with Technical Marketing, Engineering, and early customers to turn benchmarks and first production deployments into credible proof.

Shape the Product: Act as a strategic partner to Product in building the product that will win in AI inference. Bring customer and market evidence into decisions about which inference bets to pursue, what to build, and for whom.

Test, Launch, and Learn: Lead product marketing for new inference capabilities, integrations, and solutions. Test positioning, segments, use cases, and packaging with customers and the field, and use each launch to build market presence and sharpen the story.
Create High-Impact Content: Personally develop inference content including blogs, web pages, solution briefs, presentations, and customer stories that bring the story to life.

Build the Path to Scale: As winning patterns emerge, turn them into repeatable sales plays, discovery guides, objection handling, and enablement that help Sales, Solutions Engineering, and partners win.

Strong product marketing fundamentals across customer discovery, positioning and messaging, content development, launches, and go-to-market strategy.

Working knowledge of AI inference and the infrastructure behind it, including accelerated computing, model serving, GPU memory, data infrastructure, and the performance and cost dynamics of running models in production.

Strong technical aptitude and the ability to understand infrastructure architectures, benchmarks, and product capabilities, then translate them into clear customer value for technical and business audiences.
Demonstrated ability to build quantified economic value arguments such as TCO, ROI, or cost-per-unit models, and defend them with technical and executive audiences.

Exceptional writing, storytelling, and presentation skills, with demonstrated experience personally creating high-quality content such as solution briefs, presentations, web content, blogs, whitepapers, sales tools, or similar assets.

lever:twingate:63d93175-4b9e-46d3-9cb2-1.summary:
For thirty years, securing access to a company's systems has meant making them harder to use. The VPN is the clearest example: a tunnel into the whole network, slow for the people who need it and trusted far more than it deserves. The industry's answer has been more layers and more acronyms. We think that is the wrong direction.

Twingate exists to prove that the most secure way to do something can also be the easiest. A user opens their laptop and the application is simply there. Behind that, every connection is checked against who the person is, what device they are on, and what they are allowed to reach, and nothing else is visible. Security people do not have to think about is the only kind that actually gets used.

sections.title: About Twingate
paras: We sell to IT and security teams, and increasingly to engineers: some companies embed Twingate inside their own products and platforms. From startups to large enterprises, the deal is won or lost on whether the product does what we say in the customer's real environment. That is where Solutions Engineering lives. Our customers say it better than we do: twingate.com/customers.

sections.title: The role
paras: Most solutions engineers are measured on whether the demo went well. You will be measured on whether the technical evaluation produced a decision, and on making that decision a success for the customer.

You own the technical journey for our largest and most complex opportunities, from discovery through technical close and into production. Your job is to make sure the customer ends up with what they actually need, which is rarely what they first asked for, and that the people who championed Twingate internally are proven right for having done so.

Everyone on our team takes it personally when a customer does not get real value from what we build. We want someone who shares that mindset: the kind of person who opens doors for others without expecting a thank you, and who keeps asking what a customer experience could look like if nobody had done it that way before. Our shorthand for it: good service is giving champagne when asked. Great service is giving champagne at the right moment, before being asked.

sections.title: Responsibilities
paras: Run technical evaluations that end in a decision. You and the customer agree in writing, before the work starts, on what success looks like and which requirements are deal-breakers. You keep that agreement current, call it early when a deal-breaker cannot be met, and separate what the evidence shows from what you were told.

Qualify properly, including out. Before you propose anything, you know why the customer should do anything at all, why now, and who cares. You turn vague terms into testable behavior, pull on every thread of a multi-part answer instead of acknowledging it and moving on, and find the driver behind the request rather than the solution the customer proposed. People are good at normalizing pain; you do not take "we don't have much" at face value. When we are not the right fit, you say so early.

Find and build technical champions. Behind every Twingate deployment is someone who put their credibility on the line to bring us in. Your job is to make that person successful: anticipate what they will need before they ask, give them what they need to make the case internally, and make sure the win is theirs. You give more than you get, every time.

sections.title: Qualifications
bullets: 8+ years in a customer-facing technical role, including several on enterprise deals with multiple technical stakeholders.
Technical evaluations you scoped and ran yourself that ended in a clear win or a clear, early disqualification.
Practical networking knowledge: how TCP and UDP connections are established, how DNS resolves, how TLS authenticates two parties, what NAT does to a packet, and ideally how to read a packet capture.

Hands-on with at least one major cloud, Kubernetes, and an identity provider such as Okta, Entra ID, or Google Workspace. Endpoint security and device management tools (CrowdStrike, Intune, Jamf) are a strong plus.
Scripting in Python, Bash, or PowerShell, and working with REST and GraphQL APIs. Enough to automate a test or build a small integration, not to ship software.
A structured qualification method (MEDDPICC or similar). We care less which one and more whether you can show us yours from a real deal.
Clear, succinct writing. Most of the value in this role is written.
Familiarity with zero trust network access and adjacent categories helps but is not required. We can teach the market; we cannot teach intellectual curiosity.

THIS IS AN ONSITE POSITION IN OUR HOUSTON, TX FACILITY

We are looking for a resourceful, communicative and dynamic individual to join our Supply Chain team as an Account Manager. A successful employee in this role will be able to work with RRD’s clients across various industries. This individual should be knowledgeable in Supply Chain Operations, a self-starter and team player who takes initiative, thrives in a fast-paced environment.

The Account Manager will be responsible for Operational and Analytical Account Management for one or more assigned accounts. The position will be driving force for optimized service delivery, customer value/satisfaction and continuous improvement.

sections.title: Responsibilities
bullets: Serve as the primary contact for the assigned customers.
Enhance customer relationship by working closely with customer on the development of targeted solutions and new business opportunities.
Develop and maintain in depth knowledge of customer’s business and associated supply chain requirements.
Ensure planning and inventory strategies are shared and agreed upon with customers.
Maintain accurate, complete, up-to-date customer files, in addition to detailed account history.
Consult with customers to understand business issues and goals, and works with customer to develop improved solutions to business needs.
Assist sales in the preparation of RFPs and RFQs on the accounts managed.
Maintain up to date knowledge of industry trends , new products, specifications, competitor strengths and weaknesses and communicates new information to Sales Representatives.

sections.title: Qualifications
bullets: Bachelor degree in Supply Chain, Operations, Management or discipline related to functional work
5+ years of relevant work experience OR demonstrated ability to meet the job requirements.
At least 1-2 years in a Supply Chain environment is preferred.
Prior experience in a customer-facing role is required.
Must have excellent Excel skills.
Experience with Google Suite is strongly preferred.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills required.
Ability to work well with large and diverse teams across multiple time-zones.

sections.title: Additional Information
paras: RRD's current salary range for this role is $64,000 to $98,400 / year. The salary range may be adjusted based on the applicable geographic location of the hired employee, and the range may change in the future. At RRD, it is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the range for their role and compensation decisions may vary based upon, but not limited to education, skills, experience, proficiency, performance, shift and location. Depending on the role, in addition to base salary, the total compensation package may also include participation in a bonus, commission or incentive program. RRD’s benefit offerings include medical, dental, and vision coverage, paid time off, disability insurance, 401(k) with company match, life insurance and other voluntary supplemental insurance coverages, plus parental leave, adoption assistance, tuition assistance and employer/partner discounts.

At RRD, we value innovation, authenticity, and integrity. To uphold the security and fairness of our hiring process, we ask that candidates refrain from using AI tools during interviews to ensure an authentic and secure experience. We appreciate your cooperation as we work to maintain a transparent and equitable hiring process.
All employment offers are contingent upon the successful completion of both a pre-employment background and drug screen.

smartrecruiters:servicenow:7440001594784.summary: This role is on Service CRM team with responsibilities including:

sections.title: GTM Activation
bullets: Partner with Sales, Demand Gen, and Field Marketing to make sure messaging actually travels — not just to decks, but to deals
Build launch plans and run them. Own the milestones, drive the cross-functional coordination, close out the execution

sections.title: Sales Enablement
bullets: Create the tools sellers use every day — pitch decks, talk tracks, battle cards, discovery frameworks, competitive objection handlers
Run enablement sessions that actually stick — live training, recorded content, whatever format gets adoption
Work closely with sales leadership and frontline reps to understand what's working in market and what's not

sections.title: Competitive Intelligence
bullets: Know how ServiceNow stacks up against the competition and the broader field across customer service and field service — and build content that arms sellers to win
Track market moves, synthesize what matters, and get it in front of the right people quickly

sections.title: Content & Programs
bullets: Build assets across the full funnel — thought leadership, event programs, customer stories, analyst materials
Prioritize ruthlessly. You'll have a lot on your plate; knowing what to say no to is as important as knowing what to build
